name: Marginal Zone Lymphoma
aliases: Extranodal Marginal Zone B-cell Lymphoma of Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of clonal B-cell proliferation with marginal zone differentiation on lymph node or extranodal tissue biopsy
Immunophenotypic profile showing CD20+, CD5-, CD10-, BCL6- B-cells
Detection of characteristic genetic abnormalities such as t(11;18)(q21;q21) API2-MALT1 fusion in extranodal MZL
Localized or disseminated lymphadenopathy or extranodal mass consistent with marginal zone lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic confirmation of clonal marginal zone B-cell proliferation with supportive immunophenotyping; molecular genetics supportive but not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other B-cell lymphomas and correlation with clinical and radiologic findings.

searchTerms: localized lymph node enlargement without pain

pathognomonic.symptomName: Extranodal mass formation in mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue
searchTerms: extranodal tumor in mucosa-associated lymph tissue
mass formation outside lymph nodes in mucosa

pathognomonic.symptomName: Splenomegaly with circulating villous lymphocytes (in splenic MZL subtype)
searchTerms: big spleen and circulating abnormal lymph cells

common.symptomName: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Chronic gastrointestinal discomfort or ulceration (in gastric MALT lymphoma)

searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells
bone marrow not making enough cells
marrow failure causing low blood counts

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing villous lymphocytes (splenic MZL)
Anemia and cytopenias in advanced disease
imaging: CT or PET-CT showing localized or disseminated lymphadenopathy
Splenomegaly on abdominal ultrasound or CT
Extranodal masses in affected organs (e.g., stomach, salivary glands)
genetic: t(11;18)(q21;q21) API2-MALT1 fusion gene in extranodal MZL
Other chromosomal abnormalities including trisomy 3 and 18
other: Histopathology demonstrating marginal zone B-cell infiltration
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD20, negative for CD5 and CD10

distinguishingFeatures: Typical lymphocytosis with bone marrow involvement

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging lymph nodes or masses
Unexplained persistent fever and night sweats
Signs of bone marrow failure such as severe anemia or thrombocytopenia
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Cheson BD, et al. Marginal zone lymphoma: clinical features and treatment. Hematology Am Soc Hematol Educ Program. 2017.
